findings: No new static correctness blocker found in the inspected paths.

scope_checks.admission: Both recv_many arms invalidate before cooperative accounting; push_pending never restores validity after an interrupted accounting operation.
scope_checks.deadline: The ordered fast path uses the first surviving deadline, including equal deadlines; appended out-of-order/retry records disable it and use the full cooperative minimum scan.
scope_checks.expiration: Only non-sticky queues skip expiration scans before cached earliest; sticky cancellation still checks every record.
scope_checks.split: Stats are invalidated before awaiting partition/first removal and recomputed or restored before ordinary continuation; Worker Drop restores an interrupted split.
scope_checks.drain: Accounting scans before moving accepted records and commits queue/stat changes without an intervening await.
scope_checks.tests: All previous test function names remain; nine new controls use Worker methods and count completed expiration checks/suffix rescans. The single-record Vec prefix shift still occurs and is not counted.
scope_checks.compile: All observed Worker initializers have new fields; Rust compilation and Clippy are not established by static inspection.

limits: This is source-only review; no Rust build, runtime, benchmark or release claim.
Interrupted Split supports Worker Drop, not arbitrary resumption on the same Worker; this predates the patch.

When invalid, earliest_pending_deadline returns now, which worker_wake_delay can convert to no timer; current run/take-sticky paths repair stats with purge before selecting, so this invariant deserves a real cancellation test.
The cancellation test manually appends to pending then invokes accounting; it does not drive recv_many through actual Worker::run.
Rescan counters are credited only after a complete scan; they do not measure partial scans canceled at an await or Vec shifts.
